messages.content: Write a post about why a company is investing in developer relations. Around 250 words.

**Why we're hiring a devrel team**

We shipped [product] eighteen months ago and watched something uncomfortable happen. People signed up. They read the quickstart, got a hello-world running, and then — nothing. Roughly [X]% never made a second API call.

Our first instinct was that the docs were bad. They were, in places. But the real problem showed up when [name] sat down with five customers and watched them build. Every one of them got stuck at the same place: [specific step]. Not because it was hard, but because nobody had ever written down the part where you connect it to a real system with real auth and real data that isn't clean.

That gap is not a marketing problem and you cannot patch it with a webinar. It's a craft problem, and it needs people whose job is to build with the thing in public, hit the walls, and then go fix the walls.

So we're funding a devrel team of [N], reporting into [engineering/product], not marketing. Their mandate: ship reference implementations, answer in the [Discord/forum] within a day, and file bugs against our own onboarding with the same weight as customer bugs. We'll measure them on time-to-second-call and on how many docs PRs land, not on conference talks or follower counts.

The honest version: we built something developers can use and then made them figure out the hard parts alone. This is us paying that back.

[Roles are open here.]

---

Placeholders in brackets are for you to fill — I didn't want to invent metrics or names. Tell me the company and the real numbers and I'll tighten it.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.
